newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka navy hits rebel reinforcements at sea.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka navy hits rebel reinforcements at sea.

text.p: Sri Lanka's navy sank at least seven Tamil Tiger guerrilla boats early on Wednesday when it intercepted a flotilla believed to be ferrying reinforcements to stop an army offensive in the north, military officials said.
Up to 50 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels may have been killed in the conflict off Kokkilai, 260 km (160 miles) northeast of Colombo, they said.

"There were about 15-20 terrorist boats, presumably taking reinforcements, just hugging the coast sailing south to north," a navy spokesman said. "They had deployed a few craft, including suicide boats, to give them defence."
The rebel boats were believed to be taking reinforcements to try to stall an army offensive into the LTTE's northern Wanni stronghold launched two weeks ago, military officials said.
The six-hour battle began late on Tuesday when three navy Dvora fast attack craft engaged three groups of boats of the rebels' Sea Tiger naval wing, military officials said.

"Our Dvoras destroyed one group of boats with at least four boats," one official said. "Two more Dvoras and two gunboats rushed from (the eastern base at) Trincomalee (and) joined the battle, sinking three more terrorist boats."
The official said he believed at least 50 rebels would have been killed in the battle, but the navy spokesman said they estimated 25 to 30 guerrillas died.
Three rebel boats were badly damaged, while other boats managed to get away and some beached to escape the navy attack and were bombarded by artillery, military officials said.
One sailor was wounded and three navy craft were slightly damaged in the battle, the navy spokesman said.
The navy had tightened restrictions on fishing to prevent rebels escaping by sea, he said.
A military spokesman said troops killed 16 rebels on Wednesday while consolidating positions in a two-pronged thrust into the Wanni stronghold of the LTTE.
Troops have faced fierce resistance from the rebels, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the mainly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east.

Two army divisions, consisting of some 20,000 troops, launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.

One division thrust north from Vavuniya and captured the towns of Omanthai and Rambaikulam, 17 km (10 miles) north of Vavuniya. The other broke out from the northeastern Weli Oya base and seized the town of Nedunkeni, 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya.

The Defence Ministry said at least 89 soldiers had been killed and about 145 wounded in the first two weeks of the offensive, one of the military's biggest since the war began in 1983. Hospital sources said 600 soldiers had been wounded.
The military says more than 200 rebels have been killed. The LTTE have accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening the supply route.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The rebels say the toll is higher.
